payload.text:
The original production `-demoinfo -replay` failure is inherited, not introduced by NET-04. The exact same client format-4/protocol-56 file (SHA256 646deb8984787ecb7acd066e3258c4656e70bb6fa8456660b3ef31a1476dbaf9) fails in frozen NET-02 dc5, NET-03 ad65, and NET-04 4b binaries at frame 785, zero-based record 5164, BombState tag 70, length 25. All print `Replay stopped at frame 785: Replay bomb packet queue exceeded its budget.` The external thin friend entry calls the actual compiled ReplayPlaybackSession and its existing PassiveReplaySessionHost; it does not replace the decoder. Direct reinjection prints the same stack at ReplayBombFacts.cs:111. The authority v6 file also hits the inherited passive queue at frame 682, record 4735.

The passive CLI host has a no-op Advance and no scene. ReplayBombFacts retains packets until the scene consumes them and has a fixed 2048-packet pending budget. ReplaySceneServices.cs:171 calls ApplyBombPackets; ReplayBombFacts.cs:120–134 consumes and clears the queue. Those files and PassiveReplaySessionHost are unchanged between dc5 and 4b. The CLI counts-only output drops LastError, so the original receipt did not expose the cause. None of these observations change production source or loosen a validation guard.

A separate corrected external probe enters the existing Headless simulation mode, constructs the actual compiled PassiveReplayScene, and runs its actual Step method through each original recording with normal scene services. The authority format-6 file completes 5690 steps and 40553 post-Join fact events, including all 44 timed certificate records; final result Success, no warning, pending bomb packets 0. Client0 format-4 completes 5597 steps and 37334 post-Join facts; Client1 format-4 completes 5613 steps and 37456 post-Join facts; both finish Success with pending bomb packets 0. Events exclude records consumed during Join. The frame counts and success are decoder/simulation observations, not a rendering or timing measurement.

Every scene run loaded physical ProjectPrime.dll SHA256 ab231b0305f05ab02a0e44e1f424e12e97dee08cca37ba09aa5293a02b044764, MVID 7febc0c6-ae07-4b8f-bc17-ab8e291d2cc7. The corrected external entry is separately identified as SHA256 0876e52ac1e74bf5947fdc71dc5480b151470a87fe91526b71768f543e5dcb93, MVID d188f316-523f-4e16-a608-f4788a9aab95. It is a thin entry named nettest for existing friend access, not the qualified full nettest fixture. No active NetSession, grant seeds, replacement packets, fake payment, or production mutation were introduced by the probe.

Preserved negatives: original production-decoder-attempt2 receipt/log; raw passive diagnostic receipt.json and four logs; the first external scene attempt omitted Headless.Enter and rejected before frame 0 with missing GL bindings (scene-receipt.json). The corrected attempt is scene-receipt2.json and three scene2 logs. The small entry's initial compile CS0136 and repaired logs are also retained. All recorded process groups are now independently verified absent. Source worktree remains clean at 4b4b5c451a17430fcd6fadb2fe72c56b020bd570. No new source commit or rebuild of the production client occurred.

This establishes actual file reopening and normal private scene/bomb-consumer continuation for the bounded campaign files and archive certificate decoding. It does not establish pixels, Studio presentation, native timed-channel beam reconstruction, component/victim/paid-outcome joins, exact impact validation, 99.9% coverage, or NET-04 full acceptance. The inherited passive CLI failure remains a concrete negative; it is not converted to a pass.

Raw artifacts in this directory: receipt.json, scene-receipt.json, scene-receipt2.json; 4b-client0.log, ad65-client0.log, dc5-client0.log, 4b-authority.log; 4b-authority-scene2.log, 4b-client0-scene2.log, 4b-client1-scene2.log; source/Program.cs, source/RawProgram.original.cs.txt, source/SceneProgram.attempt1.cs.txt and source/diagnostic.csproj. Original campaign files are never rewritten.
